prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Such students who do not take (A) / regular mock tests seriously fail (B) / to perform well in the actual exam. (C) / No Error (D)
options: Such students who do not take
to perform well in the actual exam.
explanation: When 'such' introduces a clause, the correlative is 'as', not 'who': 'Such students as do not take'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Such was his brilliant performance (A) / that the entire auditorium stood up (B) / to give him a roaring standing ovation. (C) / No Error (D)
options: that the entire auditorium stood up
to give him a roaring standing ovation.
explanation: No error: the emphatic 'Such was his performance that...' construction is correctly used with proper inversion.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The seasoned politician spoke in such a manner (A) / as everyone present in the press room (B) / believed his fabricated narratives blindly. (C) / No Error (D)
options: The seasoned politician spoke in such a manner
as everyone present in the press room
explanation: The correlative is 'such ... that', not 'such ... as', when expressing result. Part (B) should begin 'that everyone present in the press room'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. He gave such a long speech but everybody felt bored.
explanation: 'Such' must be completed by 'that' (such a long speech that everybody felt bored), so 'such' is wrongly used with 'but'.

prompt: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Every participant gave so outstanding performance that it became difficult to choose the winner.
explanation: 'So' cannot modify an adjective+noun combination; with a singular noun the correct correlative is 'such an outstanding performance ... that'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I have never / come to / such a kind person / like my friend.
explanation: 'Such' is completed by 'as', not 'like', so it should be 'such a kind person as my friend'.

prompt: Identify the best way to improve the underlined part of the given sentence. If there is
sentence: no improvement required, select ‘no improvement’- There was a time when it was fashionable to have a dainty dog, like as the poodles or any other tiny creature as a pet.
explanation: To give an example the correct expression is 'such as' followed by a singular countable noun with the article — 'such as a poodle'; 'like as' is unidiomatic.

prompt: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In
sentence: case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. People with Alzheimer are such forgetting as they are not able to carry out a conversation for long.
explanation: With an adjective, the correlative is 'so + adjective + that', and the adjective form is 'forgetful'; 'such ... as' is wrong here.
